premises.text: Industrial robotic arms are expensive, hard to use, and not safe enough for widespread non-factory applications
premises.evidence_span: they're expensive, they're difficult to use, and quite frankly, not that safe

premises.text: Casio delivers industrial-arm capability at roughly laptop price (~10× cheaper), with kg-scale reach, sub-mm precision, and swappable end attachments
premises.evidence_span: Casio has the capabilities of an industrial arm, but the price of a laptop

premises.text: Training is done by guiding the arm through a motion or via simple app/devices, without needing an advanced degree
premises.evidence_span: We've made Casio incredibly easy to train. Simply guide the arm through a motion that it plays back perfectly

premises.text: A novel whole-surface proximity sensor detects humans up to ~20 inches away, making the arm safe around people
premises.evidence_span: It can detect a human up to 20 inches away in any direction from any point on the arm

premises.text: Casio is a developer platform with APIs that cut complexity so web developers can code for it
premises.evidence_span: we've made Cassia a developer platform. Our APIs cut the complexity, so if you can build a website, you can code for Cassia

value.text: Make robotic arms personal, ubiquitous, and democratized for many applications beyond factories
value.evidence_span: make robotic arms as ubiquitous as computers

causal_links.evidence_span: They're the ultimate universal tool, doing anything that your arms can do, only better
a sub $5,000 arm is the holy grail of robotics
when you give people incredible tools, they can do incredible things

notes: Transcript ends mid-sentence (truncated=true). Expensive/hard/unsafe kept as one problem bundle (v1.5.1 §4.1.6). Price/capability/attachments as one product mechanism; trainability and safety sensor split as separately failable modules. Biomed/healthcare/maker application list folded as uses of the same arm (§4.1 / v1.3.1 applications rule), not separate premises. Application count traction excluded.
